name: Statue of Liberty
hook: A French gift in 214 crates, a copper skin, and a poem that named the Mother of Exiles.

facts.label: Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi
facts.statement: Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi designed the Statue of Liberty; he also sculpted the Lion of Belfort.

facts.label: the French gift
facts.statement: France gave the statue to the United States, and it crossed the Atlantic in 1885 in 214 crates aboard the frigate Isère.

facts.label: Egypt Carrying the Light to Asia
facts.statement: It was first conceived as "Egypt Carrying the Light to Asia," meant for Port Said in 1869.
associations: Egypt Carrying the Light to Asia

facts.label: the 1886 dedication
facts.statement: President Grover Cleveland dedicated it on October 28, 1886; the statue is sheathed in more than 31 tons of copper mined in Norway.

facts.label: Emma Lazarus
facts.statement: Emma Lazarus wrote The New Colossus to help fund the pedestal; the sonnet calls the statue the "Mother of Exiles."

facts.label: the torch
facts.statement: The statue's torch was displayed at the 1876 Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia before it was sent to New York.

facts.label: Planet of the Apes
facts.statement: At the end of Planet of the Apes, Charlton Heston finds the Statue of Liberty half-buried on a beach.
